findings.quoted_text: All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon delivery.

Any material change to scope, assumptions, dependencies, technical requirements, or delivery sequence should be documented in writing. A change request may describe additional fees, revised dates, or other effects before the changed work begins.
All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon delivery.
findings.explanation: Transferring intellectual property rights upon delivery rather than upon full payment means the client owns the work even if they fail to pay the final invoice, stripping you of your primary leverage.
findings.suggested_change: Modify the clause so that intellectual property rights transfer to the Client only upon receipt of full payment for the applicable Deliverables.

findings.quoted_text: Any material change to scope, assumptions, dependencies, technical requirements, or delivery sequence should be documented in writing. A change request may describe additional fees, revised dates, or other effects before the changed work begins.
findings.explanation: Using discretionary language ("should" instead of "shall") and permissive phrasing ("may describe additional fees") fails to guarantee that scope changes will be documented and appropriately compensated before work begins.
findings.suggested_change: Change "should" to "shall" and require that all scope changes must be documented in a signed change order explicitly detailing additional fees and schedule adjustments prior to commencing work.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body: Hi, I have reviewed the agreement and would like to propose a few minor adjustments before signing. - Regarding the relevant clause, transferring intellectual property rights upon delivery rather than upon full payment means you would own the work even if the final invoice is unpaid. I propose modifying the clause so that intellectual property rights transfer only upon receipt of full payment for the applicable Deliverables. - Regarding the relevant clause on changes, using discretionary phrasing fails to guarantee that scope modifications will be documented and appropriately compensated before work begins. I propose changing the wording to require that all scope changes must be documented in a signed change order explicitly detailing additional fees and schedule adjustments prior to commencing work. Best regards.
